stories.delivered_paragraph: Hackers have stolen about $130 million in cryptocurrency from Coldcard hardware-wallet users, exploiting a flaw in devices designed to keep assets offline, blockchain-security firms say. At least a dozen attackers appear to be involved, and both Galaxy Research and Elliptic consider the estimate broadly credible. The theft exposes a weak point in a product category marketed as one of the safest ways to hold crypto, amid more than $950 million lost in over 200 crypto-company hacks this year.

stories.delivered_paragraph: OpenAI agreed to pay $3.2 million to settle Justice Department allegations that it discriminated against U.S. workers by favoring temporary visa holders in hiring. The company said it disagreed with the findings but settled the case, while the DOJ said OpenAI must change its recruiting practices. The penalty puts a prominent AI employer at the center of the Trump administration’s broader effort to police companies’ use of temporary-worker visa programs.

stories.delivered_paragraph: T-Mobile is introducing EIP Flex 36, a device-financing option that lets qualifying customers spread a phone, tablet or watch’s price, sales taxes and fees over 36 months with no upfront payment. The plan carries 0% APR for a limited time and can be combined with device promotions, though T-Mobile has not said what less-qualified customers will pay. It shifts costs usually due at checkout into monthly bills, potentially making new devices easier to obtain but extending repayment.

stories.delivered_paragraph: College students are moving into retirement communities not just for cheaper housing, but to build relationships with older residents through game nights, fitness classes and other shared activities. The arrangements can offer students a quieter alternative to conventional campus housing while giving residents more social contact. Their growth points to an intergenerational response to housing costs and isolation, although the communities’ early-evening routines may not suit every student.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Crowds in Gaza City held a mass funeral for 112 Palestinians, mostly women and children, whose bodies were recently recovered from a residential block struck by Israel in November 2023. A two-week recovery operation pulled members of the Abu Sharia and Hassayna families from rubble in the Sabra neighborhood; the dead included 44 children and 38 women. The delayed burial illustrates how destruction from the early Gaza war continues to leave families searching for and identifying victims.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Ukraine released video showing a Russian drone pursuing a street vendor in the Kherson region before diving toward him and exploding. The man survived with shrapnel wounds, concussion and trauma, according to a doctor; President Volodymyr Zelensky and Ukraine’s foreign minister called the attack evidence of deliberate targeting of civilians. The footage adds to allegations that remotely operated drones are being used to terrorize residents near the front line, which Russia has not addressed in the report.

stories.delivered_paragraph: More than 170 migrants attempting to cross the English Channel were rescued after their boat caught fire, British authorities said. The UK government said all of those rescued would be returned to France rather than allowed to continue their journey to Britain. The incident underscores the continuing danger of small-boat crossings and the pressure on British and French authorities to prevent overloaded, unsafe vessels from leaving the French coast.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The European Union praised Spain’s response after about 72,000 people entered the Spanish enclave of Ceuta illegally last week, Spanish officials said. Spain says roughly 70,000 of them have since been returned to Morocco. The rapid returns have contained the immediate pressure on Ceuta, but the scale of the episode highlights the enclave’s vulnerability as a gateway into the EU and the importance of Spanish-Moroccan cooperation on migration enforcement.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Europe’s heat wave is worsening drought conditions, fueling wildfires and creating energy risks as low river levels expose old wrecks in the Danube and strain nuclear-reactor cooling systems. Greece is battling deadly fires, while the drying Danube and Rhine show how extreme heat can disrupt transport and infrastructure as well as daily life. The combination of water shortages, fire danger and power-system stress leaves governments managing several climate-linked emergencies at once.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Hangar 13’s upcoming Man of Honor expansion for Mafia: The Old Country will add side activities and missions intended to make the game’s Sicily setting feel less empty. stories.delivered_paragraph: The Killers frontman Brandon Flowers says he is questioning how much longer he wants to live as a rock star as he prepares to release his third solo album, Thrasher, on August 21. His first solo record in more than a decade arrives as he reassesses the personal cost of a career spanning over 20 years.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Science communicator Hank Green says he is stepping back from production after criticism over his use of AI, which he described as “not healthy,” though he said he used chatbots to find research sources rather than write scripts. The backlash has focused on whether a creator built on credibility can rely on systems prone to convincing falsehoods and trained on others’ work. His case spotlights a poorly understood middle ground between casual AI use and more overtly harmful dependence.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Oil prices fell nearly 5% to a three-week low after U.S. officials said talks with Iran had advanced toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude dropped below $80 a barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate fell more than 5% to $76, as markets priced in the prospect of resumed shipments as soon as this week. Officials stressed that no agreement was final, so fuel-price relief remains vulnerable to another breakdown in negotiations.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The wealthiest 20% of U.S. households are buying most new cars, with the AI-driven stock-market rally helping affluent Americans spend more on vehicles, MarketWatch reports. The pattern suggests auto demand is increasingly concentrated among buyers who have benefited from rising asset values rather than spread broadly across households. That concentration can support sales of expensive vehicles, but it also leaves the market more exposed if financial-market gains fade or affordability worsens for other consumers.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Pfizer beat quarterly estimates and raised the low end of its full-year revenue guidance, citing strength in Eliquis and other medicines. At the same time, it reduced its expected 2026 revenue from Covid products to $4 billion from roughly $5 billion. The results show Pfizer relying more heavily on its established and newer drug portfolio as the pandemic-era business continues to shrink, a central challenge for the company’s longer-term growth outlook.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Fundstrat research head Tom Lee argues U.S. stocks could reach a new high in August, identifying six possible catalysts for a further rally. The call is a market forecast rather than a confirmed trend, and the available report does not specify the full list of drivers or a target level. It reflects continued bullish sentiment after strong equity gains, but investors will still be watching economic data, corporate results and policy signals that can quickly alter that outlook.
